description:
The Keplerian transfer arc rendered on /fly has the correct endpoints (Earth at departure, destination at arrival) but the middle of the arc is on the wrong side — it goes the long way around the ellipse instead of the short half-ellipse, producing a visually incorrect bulge.

Expected: The outbound transfer arc should be the short prograde (CCW) half-ellipse from Earth to the destination: the arc's path should monotonically approach the destination's orbit (outward for Mars/Jupiter/Saturn, inward for Venus/Mercury) without looping or bulging the wrong way around the chord.

Acceptance criteria:
- The arc midpoint (index = steps/2) must lie at a heliocentric distance between r1 and r2 — i.e., between Earth's orbital radius and the destination's orbital radius — for every mission that uses transferEllipse. An arc that goes the long way around (>π sweep) places the midpoint on the wrong side of the chord, producing a distance outside the [r1, r2] interval. [code-invariant: A Keplerian half-ellipse transfer (ADR-010) sweeps the short way from p1 to p2, so heliocentric distance is monotonic between the two endpoints. A sweep >π is not the intended half-ellipse.]
- The arc must sweep in the prograde (CCW) direction: the cross product of the chord (p2−p1) with the arc's midpoint offset (mid−(p1+p2)/2) must have the same sign as a CCW-rotated chord (i.e., the arc bulges CCW-side of the chord). [code: transferEllipse docstring, src/lib/mission-arc.ts lines 138-142: 'sweeping from p1 to p2 in the CCW (prograde) direction' and 'Direction: prograde (CCW) sweep from p1's heliocentric angle to p2's heliocentric angle.' Also, desiredSweep (lines 171-174) is normalized to [0, 2π), confirming CCW intent.]
- Both endpoints must remain exactly pinned to the input positions (or within floating-point tolerance). Existing tests verify this for 36 missions; they must continue to pass after a fix. [code-invariant: transferEllipse constructs an ellipse through both input positions — both F2 candidates satisfy this. The arc is not a valid solution if endpoints drift.]

Domain facts:
- The reporter's claim that the code 'always picks F2candidates[0]' is incorrect: the code iterates both F2 candidates (lines 182-192) and selects the one minimizing |nu_sweep - desiredSweep|, not the first element.
- The two F2 candidates produce mirror-image ellipses; one is the short prograde half-ellipse (<π sweep in true anomaly), the other is the long retrograde half-ellipse (>π sweep). The current heuristic compares nu_sweep (ellipse parameter space, always in [0, 2π)) against desiredSweep (heliocentric angle gap, also in [0, 2π)), which are different geometric quantities. When the heliocentric CCW gap > π, the heuristic picks the F2 with nu_sweep > π — the long way around.
- The /plan page allows choosing Mercury and Venus as destinations (9 destinations total). Any user-created plan to Mercury or Venus, or any future Mercury/Venus library mission, would hit this bug when the destination is 'behind' Earth in CCW terms.
